target_customer: Trucking companies, especially less-than-truckload carriers, later brokers and fleets
problem: Small and mid size carriers ran orders, dispatch and profitability through phone, email, fax and spreadsheets, with admin work consuming up to half of gross margin.
business_model: B2B SaaS transportation management system subscription
product_category: Transportation management system and trucking ERP

founders.name: Justin Sky
founders.background_notes: FreightWaves (Oct 2021) names Justin Sky as CEO and co-founder. The 2016 YC post lists a Justin Hein; whether they are the same person was not confirmed.

founders.name: Alexander Luksidadi
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and the YC launch post.

founders.name: Justin Bailie
founders.background_notes: Named in the YC launch post (July 2016); FreightWaves spells the surname Bailie and Balile.

technical_complexity.rationale: Order portal, dispatch app and per order costing are standard SaaS but TMS requires many integrations and domain logic for freight.

defensibility.rationale: Operational systems of record are sticky once dispatch and billing run on them, but incumbents like McLeod and many small vendors offer similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it early; Rose Rocket stayed independent and made its first acquisition, Centro, in late 2025.

market_need_then: The 2016 YC launch post describes a fragmented industry run on phone, email and fax with admin costs up to 50% of gross margin, and many small LTL carriers unable to see per shipment profit.

branding.domain_note: roserocket.com; the YC page lists the http://roserocket.com site

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable, friendly name unusual in freight software, but sources reviewed show no press on the brand itself; the ROSEROCKET mark was registered in March 2024.

outcome_analysis: Rose Rocket sold modern TMS software to small and mid size carriers, stayed lean for years, raised a $25M Series A in 2021 and a $38M Series B in 2023, and by 2025 was acquiring a startup. Steady B2B growth in a fragmented, manual industry explains its active, growth stage status.
notes: FreightWaves says total raised $25.12M per Pitchbook, implying little earlier funding; coverage of the Series B total ($69M) is from a search summary of press coverage. BusinessWire page returned 403 so the Series B details (Scale Venture Partners lead and investor list) rest on search summaries of BusinessWire, BetaKit and FreightWaves coverage. Competitors: the YC launch post names none; McLeod and others appear only on undated or recent comparison pages, so the list is empty. Exit none: Rose Rocket acquired Centro in 2025 and remains independent. No layoffs found. Seed added with null amount: Seedtable (single database) says Ripple Ventures announced on 14 May 2020 that it led the seed, with a board seat; no source gives the amount. BetaKit's Series B story gives a 69M USD total versus 63M for the recorded Series A and B, a gap of about 6M that no source itemizes, so it is not assigned to the seed. Founder names: BetaKit's Series A article spells the third founder Justin Bailie in the text and Justine Bailie in a photo caption, so the record now uses Bailie; no source was found for Hein, and Justin Sky is confirmed as CEO by BetaKit. The YC page lists only Alexander Luksidadi.
